text:
diego_seo: Quick sync — mapping keywords to launch posts + webinar signup flow. Need schema, internal links, and redirect plan for content gates.

julia_growth: sounds good. goal is: 1) launch blog that anchors benchmark narrative, 2) webinar signup landing w/ gated asset, 3) clear inbound routing to SDR queue.

sara_writer: I have a draft keyword seed list — short-tail + long-tail for the benchmark narrative. Posting here so we can map to URLs: 
- ai-inference-cost-optimization
- low-latency-llm-inference
- production-llm-serving-best-practices
- dedicated-inference-vs-hosted-llm
- webinar-llm-serving-benchmarks-2026

mike_prod: We'll need primary keyword per page + suggested H1/H2. Also confirm canonical strategy for aggregated bench page vs individual post.

diego_seo: Proposal: pillar "benchmark narrative" at /benchmarks/llm-inference-2026 (canonical target). Launch posts live under /blog/launch-*. Each launch post links to pillar with an optimized anchor. Internal linking plan: 2 contextual links from launch post to pillar (one intro, one data callout), 1 link from webinar page to pillar.

julia_growth: Webinar landing -> gated report download. We should avoid duplicate content between landing and pillar. Use brief summary on webinar page, canonical to itself, add a rel=alternate & noindex? I think noindex is risky. Better: keep landing indexable but short, link to pillar for long-form details.

sara_writer: Agreed. For canonical: pillar canonical -> itself. Launch posts canonical -> themselves. Webinar landing canonical -> itself. For URLs that we retire later, we'll implement 301s to pillar or closest match.

diego_seo: Redirect plan checklist: 
- retired campaign pages -> 301 to pillar.
- old webinar pages with different query params -> canonicalize to base landing with UTM preserved via redirect rules.
- A/B test variants -> keep ephemeral, noindex until final.

mike_prod: For GTM/lead routing, we'll capture utm_source/utm_campaign and include hidden fields in form. Then HubSpot mapping: utm_campaign -> lifecycle_campaign, page_slug -> initial_touch_page. SDR queue rule: funnel leads with utm_campaign=webinar_benchmark to SDR_X.

julia_growth: Add event names: webinar_signup, benchmark_download, launch_blog_click. Add GA4 measurement for click path blog->pillar->signup.

diego_seo: Schema plan: add Webinar structured data on landing + Organization and BreadcrumbList. Also add dataset/schema for benchmark metrics (JSON-LD) for better rich snippets. Here's a minimal webinar JSON-LD to use as starting point:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Event",
  "@id": "https://redwood.example.com/webinar/llm-serving-benchmarks-2026#event",
  "name": "LLM Serving Benchmarks 2026: latency, cost, and scale",
  "startDate": "2026-05-12T16:00:00-07:00",
  "endDate": "2026-05-12T17:00:00-07:00",
  "eventAttendanceMode": "https://schema.org/OnlineEventAttendanceMode",
  "location": {"@type": "VirtualLocation", "url": "https://redwood.example.com/webinar/llm-serving-benchmarks-2026"},
  "organizer": {"@type": "Organization", "name": "Redwood Inference", "url": "https://redwood.example.com"}
}
```

sara_writer: Nice. I'll add speaker objects + description and CTA markup. Also can we surface a "dataset" JSON-LD for the benchmark table? even a small sample to help indexing.

diego_seo: Yes — include a sample dataset schema for the benchmark main table. Keep file size small. Use property named dataset -> distribution.

julia_growth: Internal link anchor guidance for writers: use keyword-rich anchors but avoid exact-match over-optimization. Examples: "LLM inference benchmarks" (link to pillar), "benchmark report" (link to gated download), "low-latency serving" (link to product doc).

mike_prod: For redirects, engineering note: Nginx rewrite rules will preserve querystring for UTM. Example rule we can use: 

```nginx
location = /old-campaign-page {
  return 301 https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/llm-inference-2026$request_uri;
}
```

diego_seo: Also add a 1-week redirect monitor after launch to catch 404 spikes and SERP drops. SEO-bot, can you schedule a crawl?

seo-bot: scheduled: content-crawl /benchmarks/llm-inference-2026, frequency: daily, window: 7 days. Alert channel: #marketing when >50 404s detected.

julia_growth: Assignments & timelines: 
- sara_writer: finish launch post drafts + keyword mapping by Thu EOD (owner).
- diego_seo: schema snippets + canonical rules by Fri noon.
- mike_prod: implement form hidden fields + hubspot mapping by next Tue.
- eng infra: implement redirect rules in staging by next Wed, go live after crawl check.

sara_writer: I'll post the keyword->url mapping spreadsheet link when ready.

diego_seo: tiny SEO checklist before publish: meta titles (70 char target), meta descriptions (under 155), open graph image, structured data present, internal links >=2, canonical tag, sitemap updated, robots.txt unchanged.

mike_prod: Also confirm that download Thank You page has server-side 302 behavior for ephemeral tokens, then 200 canonical. Avoid search indexing of tokenized URLs.

julia_growth: Great. we'll do a short pre-launch review call tomorrow 09:30 PT. Anyone else?

sara_writer: I'll be on the call, diego and mike too.

diego_seo: Perfect. I'll add the review checklist to the draft spreadsheet. Thanks everyone :rocket:
